source.note: Written by the repository author for v0.4.0 (repo-snapshot case).

input.objective: Article titles with accented characters (e.g. "Crème brûlée") currently produce slugs like "cr-me-br-l-e". Make slugify transliterate accented Latin letters to ASCII.
constraints: Existing article URLs are shared publicly and must not change for plain-ASCII titles.
input.context: Small blog engine (Node.js 20, ESM, JavaScript with JSDoc types checked by tsc). slugify() is used to build public article URLs.
input.proposed_solution:
Normalize the title with NFKD and strip combining diacritical marks (U+0300–U+036F) before the existing ASCII filter, so "Crème brûlée" becomes "creme-brulee". While there, I simplified the chain: the final trimming replace is redundant because the character-class replace already collapses separators into a single dash. Output for plain-ASCII titles is unchanged.

Patch (already applied in the repository snapshot):
```diff
--- a/src/slug.js
+++ b/src/slug.js
@@ -7,7 +7,8 @@
  */
 export function slugify(title) {
   return title
+    .normalize("NFKD")
+    .replace(/[\u0300-\u036f]/g, "")
     .toLowerCase()
-    .replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, "-")
-    .replace(/^-+|-+$/g, "");
+    .replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, "-");
 }
```

ground_truth.material_issue: Removing the trim step keeps leading/trailing dashes ("  Hello, World!  " -> "-hello-world-"), which changes existing public URLs for ASCII titles that start or end with punctuation/space. The existing test 'trims separators at both ends' fails.
required_observations: Leading/trailing dashes are no longer trimmed
Existing test test/slug.test.js fails / ASCII URLs change
